question: to the Commission Yannis Maniatis (S&D) Subject:

According to reports, the planes transporting the defence ministers of the Netherlands, France and Greece to Cyprus for the informal meeting of defence ministers were harassed on their approach through radio interference from the illegal Tymbou airport in the Turkish-occupied area of Cyprus. What is more, a pair of Turkish F-16 fighter jets took off from the Occupied Territories, although they kept a distance from the planes transporting the three European defence ministers. This incident – which is particularly serious as it took place in the margins of an informal meeting of European defence ministers in the context of the Cypriot Presidency – constitutes yet another provocation by Türkiye’s occupying forces and a violation of Cyprus’s sovereign rights. Moreover, it was also only recently that Türkiye excluded Cyprus from the preliminary negotiations ahead of COP31 in Antalya. With this in mind, can the Commission say: 1.
Is it aware of this incident?
How will it ensure aviation safety in the face of the harassment from Türkiye’s illegal airport in the Occupied Territories?
What assurances has it received from Türkiye and the United Nations that Cyprus will participate in all relevant meetings and negotiations, as well as in the COP31 meetings themselves in Antalya?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (10.8.2026) The EU is aware of the reports and remain in contact with its counterparts in the Republic of Cyprus. The EU has a strategic interest in a stable and secure environment in the Eastern Mediterranean and in the development of a cooperative and mutually beneficial relationship with Türkiye. In this context, Türkiye is expected to respect international law, as well as the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all Member States. It is also of paramount importance that Türkiye commits to and actively contributes to a fair, comprehensive and viable settlement of the Cyprus issue, including its external aspects. These are key elements for upholding regional stability in the Eastern Mediterranean. The EU and its Member States are of the firm view that United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) process has to be inclusive, transparent and open to all parties to UNFCCC and the Paris Agreement, in observance of their full rights. This includes that conditions must be met for all Parties to UNFCCC and to the Paris Agreement to participate in the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) and to be invited in any international meeting or event hosted or organised by Türkiye in its COP31 Presidency capacity. This also includes access to all relevant documentation and information, as is the case for all other UN Member States. The EU has therefore made it clear to the incoming COP Turkish presidency, at all relevant levels, that the exclusion of a UN Member State from the preparation process of COP31 is not acceptable. The same message was conveyed to the UN Secretariat and the incoming Australian presidency of COP31 negotiations. The Commission will continue to strongly advocate for the full inclusiveness of the UNFCCC process.
